es: Responder a un dilema con una estructura clara (postura, razón, ejemplo y matiz) y manejar una pregunta inesperada ganando tiempo con naturalidad.

teaching.en: An ethical dilemma has no perfect answer, so strike a balance: give your position first and say what it comes down to.
teaching.es: Un dilema ético no tiene respuesta perfecta, así que busca un equilibrio: da primero tu postura y di a qué se reduce todo.
teaching.explanationEs: Balance = equilibrio. It comes down to + lo esencial de la decisión.
segments: An ethical dilemma has no perfect answer, so strike a balance:
give your position first and say what it comes down to.
teaching.audioText: An ethical dilemma has no perfect answer, so strike a balance: give your position first and say what it comes down to.

teaching.en: The money from a sponsor can help a small club, but it can cut both ways if the donor expects something in return.
teaching.es: El dinero de un patrocinador puede ayudar a un club pequeño, pero puede tener su doble filo si el donante espera algo a cambio.
teaching.explanationEs: Cut both ways = tener ventajas e inconvenientes. Sponsor = patrocinador.
segments: The money from a sponsor can help a small club, but it
can cut both ways if the donor expects something in return.
teaching.audioText: The money from a sponsor can help a small club, but it can cut both ways if the donor expects something in return.

teaching.en: For instance, a sweet-drink company sponsoring a health club creates a conflict of interest that the club must acknowledge.
teaching.es: Por ejemplo, una empresa de bebidas dulces que patrocina un club de salud crea un conflicto de intereses que el club debe reconocer.
teaching.explanationEs: For instance introduce un caso concreto que sostiene la razón. Conflict of interest = conflicto de intereses.
segments: For instance, a sweet-drink company sponsoring a health club creates
a conflict of interest that the club must acknowledge.
teaching.audioText: For instance, a sweet-drink company sponsoring a health club creates a conflict of interest that the club must acknowledge.

teaching.en: Make your answer fair by granting the other side its best point, and only then say where you would draw the line.
teaching.es: Haz tu respuesta justa reconociendo el mejor punto del otro lado, y solo entonces di dónde pondrías el límite.
teaching.explanationEs: Fair = justo. Draw the line = fijar el límite que no se cruza.
segments: Make your answer fair by granting the other side its best
point, and only then say where you would draw the line.
teaching.audioText: Make your answer fair by granting the other side its best point, and only then say where you would draw the line.

teaching.en: That said, you may accept a proposal and still set one condition, because a condition refines a position without reversing it.
teaching.es: Dicho esto, puedes aceptar una propuesta y aun así poner una condición, porque una condición afina la postura sin invertirla.
teaching.explanationEs: That said abre el matiz. Una condición (provided that…) no cambia tu postura: la precisa.
segments: That said, you may accept a proposal and still set one
condition, because a condition refines a position without reversing it.
teaching.audioText: That said, you may accept a proposal and still set one condition, because a condition refines a position without reversing it.

teaching.en: If a question is unexpected, gain a moment with That is a fair point, then answer in the same four steps.
teaching.es: Si una pregunta es inesperada, gana un momento con «Es un punto acertado» y responde en los mismos cuatro pasos.
teaching.explanationEs: Frases para ganar tiempo: That is a fair point / Let me think for a moment. Después, postura, razón, ejemplo y matiz.
segments: If a question is unexpected, gain a moment with That is
a fair point, then answer in the same four steps.

prompt.es: ¿Qué respuesta sigue la estructura postura + razón + ejemplo?

choices.text: That is a difficult question, and there are many things to consider before any decision is made.
I would accept, but then again I would refuse, because both choices have clear advantages and some real disadvantages.
Banks usually sponsor events because they want attention and new customers for their services.
I would accept, because the fair needs funding; for instance, last year we had no budget for materials.

feedback.es: Es la única respuesta que toma postura, la justifica con because y aporta un ejemplo concreto con for instance. Las demás no toman postura o se contradicen.

hint.es: Busca una postura clara, una razón y un caso concreto.

origin.text: Dilemma: a bank offers to sponsor the school science fair, but it wants its name on every poster.

prompt.es: Completa: «Dicho esto, aun así aceptaría al patrocinador.»

feedback.es: That said abre el matiz: concede el punto de los padres sin cambiar la postura, que sigue siendo aceptar.

hint.es: Son dos palabras que abren un matiz; falta la primera.

origin.text: I understand why some parents oppose the plan, and I share part of their concern. ___ said, I would still accept the sponsor, provided that the club keeps control of the team.

prompt.es: Ordena: «En conjunto, yo aceptaría la oferta con dos condiciones.»

answer.text: On balance I would accept the offer with two conditions

feedback.es: On balance abre la postura sopesada y with two conditions añade el matiz sin invertirla.

hint.es: Empieza con la expresión que resume el balance de ventajas y riesgos.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cómo maneja Sara la pregunta inesperada.

choices.text: She avoids the question by changing the subject to teenagers.
She buys a moment and then answers in her usual structure.
She answers at once without considering any objection.

feedback.es: Sara usa «a fair point» para ganar tiempo y responde con postura (rechazar), razón (adolescentes) y matiz (algo neutral). No esquiva la pregunta ni responde sin pensar.

origin.audio: Asked whether her club should accept money from an oil company, Sara paused and said that this was a fair point. She explained that she would refuse, because the club works with teenagers, and that she would draw the line at any advertising near the pitch. Only then did she add that the company might give money to something neutral, such as repairing the roof.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada parte de la respuesta con su función.

pairs: For instance, the nets are broken
That said, I would set one condition

feedback.es: Cada parte cumple una función distinta: postura, razón, ejemplo y matiz.

pairs: For instance, the nets are broken
That said, I would set one condition

prompt.es: ¿Qué respuesta gana tiempo de forma natural ante la pregunta del entrevistador?

choices.text: That would never happen, so I do not really need to answer that kind of question.
Well, it depends on the amount of money, and I would decide later when we know more.
That is a fair point; let me think for a moment.

feedback.es: Reconocer el punto y pedir un momento es una forma natural de ganar tiempo antes de responder. Las otras dos esquivan la pregunta o evitan tomar postura.

origin.text: Interviewer: Would you still accept the money if the sponsor asked you to drop one player from the team?

prompt.es: Responde al dilema como si hablaras dos minutos y contesta a la pregunta inesperada.

answer.text: To begin with, I would accept the sponsor, because our club needs new equipment and the school cannot pay for it. For instance, the nets are broken, and half of the balls are old. On balance, I think the benefits outweigh the risks, although I see the dilemma: the café sells sweet drinks, and our club is about health. It comes down to whether we can accept the money without losing our values. That said, I would set two conditions. First, the café must also sell water and fruit at our events. Second, the sponsor cannot decide anything about the team. As for your question about the logo, that is a fair point. Let me think for a moment. I would accept a small logo on the shirts, provided that the players agree and the logo stays small. That is where I would draw the line: no advertising during matches. In short, I would say yes, but only with clear limits, and I would review the agreement at the end of the season.
accepted: To begin with, I would accept the sponsor, because our club needs new equipment and the school cannot pay for it. For instance, the nets are broken, and half of the balls are old. On balance, I think the benefits outweigh the risks, although I see the dilemma: the café sells sweet drinks, and our club is about health. It comes down to whether we can accept the money without losing our values. That said, I would set two conditions. First, the café must also sell water and fruit at our events. Second, the sponsor cannot decide anything about the team. As for your question about the logo, that is a fair point. Let me think for a moment. I would accept a small logo on the shirts, provided that the players agree and the logo stays small. That is where I would draw the line: no advertising during matches. In short, I would say yes, but only with clear limits, and I would review the agreement at the end of the season.

My position is that we should accept the money. The club is small, and it needs new equipment. For example, we have only one good ball, and the shirts are very old. The school cannot pay for new things, so the help of a sponsor is important to us. Although the café sells sweet drinks, we can ask it to offer water as well. It comes down to trust: if the sponsor respects our conditions, the agreement can work. That said, I would want a written agreement, because the sponsor should not choose our team. About the logo, good question. Let me think. I would accept it on the shirts, as long as the players agree, but I would draw the line at advertising during matches. I would also ask the players and the families for their opinion before we sign anything. Overall, I would say yes, with clear limits.

feedback.es: Una respuesta completa da la postura, la razón con un ejemplo, un matiz con condiciones y contesta la pregunta inesperada con calma y en la misma estructura.

origin.text: Dilema: un café local ofrece patrocinar el club deportivo de tu escuela, pero vende bebidas dulces. Responde como si hablaras durante dos minutos: postura, razón con ejemplo y matiz. Después contesta a la pregunta inesperada: «¿Y si el café quisiera poner su logotipo en las camisetas?»

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué muestra la última frase de la hablante.

choices.text: That her acceptance comes with a limit she will not cross.
That she has changed her mind about accepting the money.
That she believes the company's name is not a problem for young people.

feedback.es: «That said, I would insist…» añade una condición sin cambiar la postura: acepta, pero con un límite. No rectifica ni cree inocua la marca.

origin.audio: Some people say that a sports club should never accept money from a company that sells fast food, and I see the risk. But I would argue that refusing would hurt the children more than the company's name would, because the club is small and its members are young. For instance, last year our club cancelled two tournaments for lack of funds. That said, I would insist that the company does not appear on the children's shirts.

prompt.es: ¿Qué respuesta mantiene la estructura ante la pregunta inesperada?

choices.text: That is a very interesting question, and I thank you for it, and many people have different views on this topic.
I would say no. The captain speaks for the players, not the donor; for instance, the players vote for theirs each year.
It depends. Sometimes sponsors are helpful, and sometimes they are not, so it is honestly very difficult to say either way, in my opinion.

feedback.es: Toma postura (no), la razona (el capitán habla por los jugadores) y da un ejemplo. Las otras se quedan en cortesía o en «it depends».

origin.text: Interviewer: What if the sponsor wanted to choose the team captain?

prompt.es: Completa: «Pondría el límite en que el patrocinador elija a los jugadores.»

feedback.es: Draw the line at + acción es la colocación fija para fijar el límite que no se cruza.

origin.text: I would gladly take the money and help the club, but I would ___ the line at letting the sponsor choose the players.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué da a entender la respuesta de Mia sobre su postura.

choices.text: That it is uncertain: she has no position and waits for the costs.
That it is opposed: she uses the question to attack the plan.
That it is firm but conditional: students must pay nothing extra.

feedback.es: Mia dice «yes» y fija una condición: que el sobrecoste no recaiga en los estudiantes. Es firme pero condicionada. No duda ni ataca el plan.

origin.audio: Halfway through her presentation, a teacher asked Mia whether she would still support the plan if it cost twice as much. Mia smiled, said that it was a fair point and that she needed a moment. Then she answered: yes, provided that the extra cost came from the sponsor and not from students, because it comes down to who pays for the risk.

prompt.es: ¿Qué corrección aplica la estructura completa a esta respuesta?

choices.text: On balance I would accept, because the club needs funds; for instance, our nets are broken. That said, I would set a condition.
I would accept. The club needs funds. The nets are broken. I set a condition. That is all I wish to say about it, thank you.
Sponsors have advantages, and they also have disadvantages, but on balance both sides of the question are equally important to consider.

feedback.es: Toma postura, la razona, da un ejemplo y añade un matiz. La versión de frases sueltas carece de conectores y la que describe ventajas e inconvenientes no decide nada.

origin.text: Well, it is difficult. Some people like sponsors, and others do not, and there are good points on both sides, and in my opinion it is hard to say.

prompt.es: Escribe en inglés: «Dicho esto, pondría el límite en la publicidad durante los partidos.»

answer.text: That said, I would draw the line at advertising during matches.
accepted: That said, I would draw the line at advertising during matches.
That said, I would set a limit: no advertising during matches.
However, I would draw the line at advertising during matches.

feedback.es: That said abre el matiz y draw the line at + nombre fija el límite que no se cruza.

origin.text: Dicho esto, pondría el límite en la publicidad durante los partidos.
